column1: # Story Run quest arcs that unlock Rare and Exceptional Remembrance lines (Design v2 Part II "Rarity categories", the roster's
# unlock routes). Built by tools/story/build-quest-arcs.mjs. One row per scene, in order; the last scene of an arc unlocks.
# arc|unlocks (Remembrance ids, comma)|act|beat 1|beat 2

stranded_dragonair|rm_dratini|2|A fisher at the lake shore says a Dragonair has been circling the same rocks for days, too weak to leave.|You find it caught in an old net, scales dull. It does not flee when you come close.

stranded_dragonair|rm_dratini|3|You bring berries and clean water each time you pass. The Dragonair's scales start to shine again.|Today it slips free of the last strands of net and rises over the water, calling once.

stranded_dragonair|rm_dratini|4|At the lake's edge a small Dratini waits where the Dragonair used to circle.|The Dragonair watches from the water as the Dratini follows you. It seems to be saying thank you. Dratini can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

peak_alpha|rm_bagon|3|Climbers whisper about an Alpha that rules the highest peak, and a little Bagon that keeps leaping at it from the cliffs.|You climb until the air is thin. On the summit the Alpha roars, and the Bagon jumps again.

peak_alpha|rm_bagon|4|You face the Alpha together with the tiny Bagon at your side. When the dust settles, the Alpha bows its head and leaves the peak.|Bagon stands at the cliff edge and, for once, does not jump. It looks at you instead. Bagon can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

ironvein_prototype|rm_beldum|2|In an abandoned Ironvein Combine lab, one console is still blinking. Something metal hums behind the glass.|A Beldum floats in a sealed chamber, labelled PROTOTYPE 0. Its eye follows you.

ironvein_prototype|rm_beldum|3|You find the lab's override code in a dusty notebook. The chamber hisses open.|Beldum hovers out, studies you for a long moment, and settles beside you. Beldum can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.
fed_three_nights|rm_gible|2|A wild Gible keeps watching your camp from a sandy burrow, too wary to come close.|You leave a share of food at the burrow's mouth. In the morning it is gone.
fed_three_nights|rm_gible|3|The Gible is back, closer this time. You leave food again, and it eats while you watch.|It bites your bag on the way out. You decide to take that as friendship.

fed_three_nights|rm_gible|4|On the third night the Gible walks right into camp and curls up by the fire.|It is still asleep there when you pack up, and it follows you down the road. Gible can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

choir_ritual|rm_deino|3|At a Hollow Choir ritual site, the singing stops when you arrive. In the middle of the circle, a feral Deino is chained to a stone.|The chanters scatter into the dark. The Deino snaps at every sound.

choir_ritual|rm_deino|4|You speak to it, softly, until it stops snapping and listens to your voice. The chain falls away.|Deino follows the sound of your steps out of the ruin. Deino can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.
rain_night|rm_goomy|2|On a night of heavy rain, something small and slimy is huddled under your tent flap.|A Goomy, shivering, though it is made of rain. It seems to have run from a bigger Pokémon.

rain_night|rm_goomy|3|You let it stay dry beside you until morning. When the rain stops, it does not leave.|Goomy slides after you, leaving a shiny trail, and seems quite proud of it. Goomy can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

training_camp|rm_jangmo_o|3|Your rival invites you to a mountain training camp. A young Jangmo-o is challenging every Pokémon there.|Your rival grins. "That one has fire. Think you can keep up with it?"

training_camp|rm_jangmo_o|4|You train with the Jangmo-o for three days. On the last, it clangs its scales at you and refuses to stay behind.|Your rival laughs. "Looks like it picked you." Jangmo-o can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.
lost_dreepy|rm_dreepy|2|At dusk a Dreepy drifts into camp, looking for something it cannot name.|It keeps floating toward the hills, then back to you, as if asking you to come.
lost_dreepy|rm_dreepy|3|You follow it to an old shrine, lit by ghost-fire. Other Dreepy flicker in the dark.|One of them is its parent, a tired Dragapult. The family circles you once.

lost_dreepy|rm_dreepy|4|The Dragapult sends the little Dreepy back to you. It has decided you are its family now too.|Dreepy settles in your bag as if it has always been there. Dreepy can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

long_winter|rm_frigibax|3|Snow falls in the middle of summer on a mountain route. People call it the Long Winter, and they say a Frigibax causes it.|You find an Alpha Baxcalibur guarding the pass, and a small Frigibax hiding behind it.

long_winter|rm_frigibax|4|The Alpha is old and tired. When you stand your ground, it lets the snow stop and lies down to rest.|The little Frigibax waddles to you, and the pass begins to thaw. Frigibax can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.
lucky_egg|rm_togepi|2|A Pokémon Breeder hands you a spotted egg. "It needs a calm road and a kind team. Can you carry it a while?"|The egg is warm and wobbles when the team is near.
lucky_egg|rm_togepi|3|You keep the egg close through every fight, never letting it get bumped.|At night you can hear a faint tapping from inside.

lucky_egg|rm_togepi|4|The shell cracks open and a Togepi tumbles out, giggling at the first thing it sees: you.|The Breeder smiles. "It chose well." Togepi can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.
twin_burrow|rm_nidoran_f|2|A sinkhole has opened in a field. Two Nidoran, one blue and one purple, are trapped at the bottom.|They are trying to push each other up and both keep sliding back down.

twin_burrow|rm_nidoran_f|3|You lower a rope and lift them out, one after the other. They will not leave each other's side.|Both of them follow you, and neither will go without the other. Nidoran♀ and Nidoran♂ can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

lantern_vigil|rm_duskull|2|In an old graveyard, the lanterns go out one by one each night. A caretaker asks you to keep the first one lit.|You keep watch. Near midnight, a Duskull drifts by and stares into your lantern.
lantern_vigil|rm_duskull|3|At the second lantern the Duskull is waiting for you. It helps you keep the flame from the wind.|The caretaker says nobody has seen a Duskull help before.

lantern_vigil|rm_duskull|4|At the last lantern, the Duskull shows you an old grave with your family's name on it, then waits beside you.|When dawn comes, it follows you out of the graveyard. Duskull can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

retired_uniform|rm_pawniard|3|After you beat a squad of grunts, a Pawniard steps out of their camp, wearing a scrap of an old team uniform.|It salutes you, the way it was taught to salute its old boss.

retired_uniform|rm_pawniard|4|You take the scrap of uniform from it and fold it away. The Pawniard looks lost, then stands at your side instead.|It does not wait for orders. It chose you. Pawniard can now be found in the Remembrance Archive.

crowded_shelter|rm_eevee|2|A shelter keeper has a basket of Eevee kits and a rule: each goes only to someone it chooses. They crowd your boots, all but one, who watches from the rafters.|You sit still and say nothing. The quiet one climbs down on its own and tests your sleeve with a paw.

crowded_shelter|rm_eevee|3|The keeper shows you the quiet one's papers: three owners returned it, always for being too careful. It looks at you as if to ask whether you will do the same.|You promise nothing aloud and sign anyway. The Eevee takes a stone from the shelf, drops it in your hand and does not let go of your sleeve all day.

static_lullaby|rm_toxel|2|An old generator hall hums all night. Inside, a Toxel is curled against the warm casing, sparking softly whenever the dynamo skips a beat.|The caretaker says the hall was built to keep the little ones calm. You drag a lamp over and match the dynamo's rhythm by tapping your knee.

static_lullaby|rm_toxel|3|By dawn the Toxel is tapping along. A bright spark leaps from its back to your palm and does not hurt.|The caretaker switches off the dynamo for the first time in years. The Toxel hums on alone, and then follows you out the door.

fossil_in_the_wall|rm_shieldon|2|Masons repairing a hill fort break open a wall and find a slab with a shape pressed into it. A lab courier takes it for the revival machine and asks you to carry the case.|The machine hums and cracks the slab. Out stumbles a Shieldon that squares up against the first thing it sees, which is you.

fossil_in_the_wall|rm_shieldon|3|It will not leave your side of the road, always placing itself between you and the open ground. The courier laughs and says it thinks it is still on guard duty.|You tell it the watch is over. It thinks about this, sits down in the road and leans its whole weight against your leg.

challengers_horn|rm_nidoran_m|2|In a meadow a young Nidoran does the same thing to every Pokemon that wanders past: puffs up, squeaks a challenge and gets knocked flat.|You offer a friendly bout. It loses in four seconds and is on its feet again before you finish saying well fought.

challengers_horn|rm_nidoran_m|3|Back at dusk it has brought a bigger challenge, a boulder it plainly cannot move. It shoves anyway, hour after hour, until the stone shifts one inch.|It looks up at you, chest heaving, hornless and delighted. When you start walking, it trots after you, already squeaking at the next thing in the road.

debug_lounge|rm_porygon|2|A dim lounge in a lab basin has one occupied terminal. A Porygon repeats the same three steps on its screen forever, and the staff say the loop has run since last season.|You read the three steps aloud and notice the second one points back at the first. It is not broken. It is waiting for someone to say stop.

debug_lounge|rm_porygon|3|You type the word stop. The loop ends and the Porygon spins, then writes your name on the screen in blocky letters.|It copies a tiny file onto your phone: a map of every lab exit it has ever walked. The staff say it is yours now and the terminal has never looked so quiet.

hive_edge_camp|rm_weedle|2|A ranger camp sits at the edge of a hive-thick wood. The rangers wear thick gloves and treat the Weedle underfoot with great respect.|A ranger explains that the young ones guard the camp stores. One has stuck itself to your boot and will not let go of the laces.

hive_edge_camp|rm_weedle|3|At night the camp is raided by something large in the dark. The Weedle that picked you stands up on its little legs and holds the line with a stinger the size of a pin.|In the morning the rangers hang a camp ribbon on its back. It would sooner stay with you than wear it, so you tie it to your pack instead.

cocoon_season|rm_caterpie|2|It is cocoon season in the glade: every branch hangs heavy with silk. A Caterpie below one tree has rolled itself into a ball, shivering, plainly afraid to start.|You sit beside it through the afternoon and read out loud from a worn paperback. It uncurls an inch at a time.

cocoon_season|rm_caterpie|3|Nightfall brings a cold wind and the cocoons begin to sway. You use your coat as a windbreak for the whole row, and the Caterpie spins its first thread to hold the coat in place.|By morning every cocoon is still hanging. The Caterpie, tired and proud, climbs your sleeve and spins a thread from your wrist to its branch before it falls asleep.

tadpole_races|rm_poliwag|2|A village pond holds the Tadpole Races each season. The Poliwag line up on a rope in a splashing, giggling row.|One lane is empty because its Poliwag keeps swirling instead of racing. The judges shrug. You call its name and it paddles straight into your hands.

tadpole_races|rm_poliwag|3|The race starts. Your Poliwag swims the course in a spiral, dizzying the whole field, and finishes last by a mile with the biggest grin of the day.|The judges award it a ribbon for Best Spin. It wears the ribbon on its belly swirl and follows you home down the creek.

midnight_bloom|rm_oddish|2|A florist swears a bloom opens in the meadow only at midnight, and only for someone who does not pick it. You wait on the grass as the stars come out.|A small Oddish pushes up out of the soil beside you, rubbing sleep from its leaves. It points at the sky.

midnight_bloom|rm_oddish|3|At the stroke of midnight the whole meadow opens at once, pale and glowing. The Oddish dances through the petals and the pollen drifts like slow snow.|You do not pick a single flower. At dawn the Oddish is still dancing, and the florist says the meadow has never bloomed so brightly.

hollow_station|rm_ralts|2|The last train left the hollow station years ago, but a Ralts still waits on platform two, head cocked, as if listening to a crowd.|It tugs your sleeve and points at the empty benches. You sit down where it points and for a moment feel the ghost of a busy morning.

hollow_station|rm_ralts|3|The Ralts shares every feeling it has caught from the platform: a goodbye, a lost ticket, a reunion, one tired person who just wanted a seat. It does not seem to mind carrying them.|You tell it it can put some of them down. It stares for a long time, then climbs into your arms, lighter, and rests its head on your shoulder.

scarred_hide|rm_sandile|2|Out in the dry flats, a Sandile with a long scar across its hide slides along a ridge, always staying exactly one dune ahead of you.|A sandstorm rolls in. The Sandile does not wait. It leads you through the swirling dust by flicking its tail at hidden rocks.

scarred_hide|rm_sandile|3|The storm clears at a dry well. The Sandile drinks first, then looks at you and pushes the shallow pool over with its snout.|It shows you the scar, a clean old line, and lets you sit beside the well. When you leave the flats, it walks just behind your heel.
